title: Vikram Agrawal v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Dilip B. Bhosale, C.J. and Yashwant Varma, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; fresh Annexure 4.2 application to be considered
headnote: A new connection had been refused for want of proved title and because a civil dispute was pending. The High Court disposed of the writ by permitting a fresh application with a duly executed Annexure 4.2 indemnity bond under Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The licensee was to scrutinise any such application made within the time allowed and pass appropriate orders; the 6 April 2017 refusal was rendered ineffective. Connection was not directed on the merits.
facts: The petitioner sought a new permanent connection from Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. The licensee refused, holding that he had not proved title to the premises and that a civil dispute with his father was pending. He argued that the dispute could not block a connection if he met the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The licensee invoked Clause 4.4 and Annexure 4.2, saying an indemnity bond would allow the application to be considered afresh. He undertook to apply with that bond.

holding_units.topic: new connection — indemnity bond where title is disputed
holding_units.holding: An applicant refused a new connection for want of proved title, and because a civil dispute is pending, may apply afresh with a duly executed indemnity bond in the form of Annexure 4.2 to Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the licensee shall then scrutinise the application and pass appropriate orders, and the earlier refusal stands ineffective. No connection is directed on the merits.

not_decided.point: Whether the petitioner is entitled to a new connection on the merits, including title and the pending civil dispute with his father
not_decided.note: The Court directed only scrutiny and appropriate orders on a fresh Annexure 4.2 application.
